author: Jim Walsh
title: Luxury apartments open at Moorestown Mall site - NewsBreak
text:
By Jim Walsh ,
1 days ago
A long-awaited apartment complex has opened at Moorestown Mall even as construction continues on more homes.
The Pearl Apartments is welcoming the first tenants for approximately 85 leased units at what's to ultimately be a 375-home complex in a former parking lot between a Boscov's store and Nixon Drive.
"We are standing at the beginning of a new community," Thomas Leonard III, chairman of the project's developer, Bel Canto Asset Growth Fund, said at a ribbon-cutting ceremony Sept. 22.
The luxury apartments are to offer amenities such as 9-foot ceilings, "chef-inspired" kitchens, and in-home washers and dryers.
Current amenities include coworking spaces, a podcasting studio and an outdoor "reflection court." Once completed, likely next year, the seven-building site is to include a swimming pool with a sun deck and a fitness center with yoga spaces.
But rents might strike some as eye-popping.
Monthly payments start at $2,299 for a 554-square-foot studio and $4,669 for a 1,269-square-foot three-bedroom, according to a spokesperson.
Rent would start at $5,399 for the largest unit, a 1,410-square foot home with three bedrooms and three baths.
The rent doesn't cover utilities. Tenants can also expect fees for garage parking, trash removal and other services.
The complex offers 15 floor plans for studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom layouts.
The apartment complex, to include 75 affordable unit for low-income tenants, opened after a years-long challenge for Bel Canto.
The suburban Philadelphia firm bought the six-acre site in a mall parking lot for $11.8 million in 2022. The mall's owner, PREIT of Philadelphia, appeared to be eager to pay down debt and diversify its tenant mix.
Bel Canto prepared infrastructure and a four-story garage before rising interest rates put the project on hold in early 2024.
The developer took advantage of a dip in lending costs to obtain a $95.8-million construction loan in July 2025. It held a ground-breaking ceremony two months later.
"For a long time, Pearl Apartments was an idea, a vision discussed in meetings, refined in plans and drawings," Leonard told an audience in a two-story leasing lounge with a glass-fronted gas-fueled fireplace.
"And today that vision has become real."
Jim Walsh is a senior reporter with the Courier-Post, Burlington County Times and The Daily Journal. Email: Jwalsh@cpsj.com.
This article originally appeared on Cherry Hill Courier-Post: Luxury apartments open at Moorestown Mall site
